price-per-square-foot-calculator.quickAnswer: Price per square foot = total price / area in square feet. Example: a property listed at 8,500,000 for 1,200 sq ft costs 7,083.33 per sq ft, which is 76,244.29 per sq m. Unit price lets you compare a 900 sq ft flat with a 1,400 sq ft one on equal footing, but it never captures location, condition, or layout differences.
keyFacts: Unit price divides the total price by the area, so different-sized properties become comparable.
Always compare carpet area with carpet area, or built-up with built-up: mixing them misleads.

Price per sq ft varies hugely by micro-location, floor, facing, and age of the building.
New launches often quote a lower per-sq-ft price but on inflated super built-up area.
Unit price is a screening tool, not a valuation: two flats at the same rate can differ wildly in value.

price-per-square-foot-calculator.formula:
Price per sq ft = Total price / Area in sq ft.
Price per sq m = Price per sq ft x 10.7639.
Price per sq yd = Price per sq ft x 9.
Example: 8,500,000 / 1,200 = 7,083.33 per sq ft.
price-per-square-foot-calculator.workedExample:
Price 8,500,000, area 1,200 sq ft:
1. Price per sq ft: 8,500,000 / 1,200 = 7,083.33.
2. Price per sq m: 7,083.33 x 10.7639 = 76,244.29.
3. Price per sq yd: 7,083.33 x 9 = 63,750.00.
A second listing at 9,900,000 for 1,400 sq ft = 7,071.43 per sq ft, slightly cheaper per unit despite the higher total.

faqs.q: What is a good price per square foot?
faqs.a: There is no universal good number: it depends entirely on the city and micro-location. Research recent sales of similar flats in the same neighborhood, then compare your listing's unit price against that local benchmark.

faqs.q: Carpet area vs built-up area: which should I use?
faqs.a: Carpet area, the actual usable floor inside the walls, whenever the listing provides it. Built-up adds wall thickness and balconies; super built-up adds a share of common areas. The same flat looks cheaper per sq ft on super built-up area, which is why builders prefer quoting it.

faqs.q: Why do two identical flats have different per-sq-ft prices?
faqs.a: Floor rise premiums, facing (park or road), corner units, furnishing, distress sales, and negotiation all move the number. Unit price starts the comparison; it never finishes it.

faqs.q: Does a lower price per sq ft always mean a better deal?
faqs.a: No. It can mean a worse location, an older building, legal issues, or poor construction. Treat a surprisingly low unit price as a reason to investigate, not a reason to celebrate.

faqs.q: How do I convert between sq ft, sq m, and sq yd?
faqs.a: Multiply: 1 sq m equals 10.7639 sq ft, and 1 sq yd equals 9 sq ft. The calculator shows all three automatically from the sq ft figure.

faqs.q: Should I include stamp duty and registration in the price?
faqs.a: For comparing listings, use the quoted price so every listing is treated the same. For your own budget, add 5 to 10% for stamp duty, registration, and brokerage on top of the unit-price math.
